text.en: Believing the giant dipole resonance is a single nucleon (or a small handful of nucleons) individually absorbing an incoming photon, similar to how an atomic electron absorbs a photon in an atomic transition -- the resonance is instead a genuinely collective, bulk oscillation involving essentially all of the nucleus's protons moving together against essentially all of its neutrons, a coherent motion of the nuclear liquid drop as a whole; this collective character, not any single-nucleon transition, is why the resonance is so broad, so strong, and so universally present across nearly every nucleus.
text.et: Arvamus, et hiiddipoolresonants on üksik nukloon (või väike käputäis nukloone) individuaalselt sissetuleva footoni neelamas, sarnaselt sellega, kuidas aatomi elektron neelab footoni aatomi ülemineku käigus -- resonants on selle asemel tõeliselt kollektiivne, massiline võnkumine, mis hõlmab sisuliselt kõiki tuuma prootoneid liikumas koos kõigi selle neutronite vastu, tuuma vedelikutilga koherentne liikumine tervikuna; just see kollektiivne iseloom, mitte mistahes üksiku nukloni üleminek, on põhjus, miks resonants on nii lai, nii tugev ja nii universaalselt kohal peaaegu igas tuumas.
